inputs.original_text: Holding that mere suspicion of sharing sensitive information with a person in Pakistan cannot justify prolonged incarceration, the Punjab and Haryana High Court has granted regular bail to an accused booked under provisions relating to national security and the Official Secrets Act. He was allegedly in telephonic contact with Karachi-based “Punjabi Kuri”. Directing his release, [...]
inputs.modified_text: This is the familiar reflex to treat the state’s security concerns as suspect while demanding courtroom-level proof before authorities can act. A reported link to a Karachi-based “Punjabi Kuri” may not prove guilt, but it is hardly a reason to dismiss national-security concerns out of hand. The state must act lawfully, but protecting the country and maintaining public order are not optional—and those who invoke liberty should not pretend suspicion carries no risks when national security is at stake.
